item.title: MAN. I think dead internet theory is correct, I think the adage "if it feels too good to be true" needs to be followed closely, and that nothing online is trustworthy now means after 40 years of being online, it's going to make me stop using the internet.
item.description:
FAKE. I fell in love with this cute pup on an instagram my wife sent. I fully believed it for about a minute... then looked at the account selling the life vest, which had dozens and dozens of IDENTICAL videos with different dog breeds. 85 posts in one month. Impossible. The company is new, the website is sketchy, it's all social media AI Slop ad scams on instagram. it's CRAZY. But I really couldn't tell for a bit, and I'm not lazy or bad at this. But I don't want to use the internet where you have to doubt everything for minutes at a time.
If people create something with no effort, it has no value. Why would I want to be subjected to this slop without my consent? What in the hell are platforms thinking? What are these technologists thinking... because they're ruining the internet. And one giddy bad actor can launch score of these fake website companies, exponentially destroying the usability of the internet. When the utility of the internet is broken, and you need to spend 10 minutes figuring out if a harmless, meaningless video is real... It is as over as shell art. Cooked, as they say. It's pretty surreal how quickly the internet degraded. First enshittification, then organic search... but holy crap it's unusable. Why is Silicon Valley constantly answering questions no one asked? Weirdos.

item.title: GovBrief Today #568
item.description: Donald Trump threatened to sue a think tank for $5 billion over numbers it published. The Center for American Progress measured crime in Washington, Los Angeles, and Memphis and found his National Guard deployments didn't change the crime rate. His personal lawyer, not the White House counsel, sent a nine-page letter threatening the suit unless CAP retracted the report, apologized, and paid Trump money by Friday evening, closing with "PLEASE GOVERN YOURSELVES ACCORDINGLY." The letter offers no competing crime numbers. CAP refused. That deadline expired the same day the Pentagon fired three Stars and Stripes journalists, citing the editor for telling CBS that censoring news to service members would be a red line. The Trump administration doesn't argue that facts are wrong, only what you'll pay for saying them out loud. I've emailed 8,755 stories over 568 straight nights, free and without ads. The algorithm can't show them all to you. Add your email address at govbrief.today and I will. item.title: Trade deal trap.
item.description: ​"Divide et impera" Application: A foundational Roman diplomatic strategy used in treaty-making. Rome would isolate trading partners or allied city-states through bilateral agreements, preventing them from forming unified economic or defensive blocs, effectively trapping them in a dependent status one by one. I am going to say Trump tried to kill Carney's ​"Middle powers must act together, because if you're not at the table, you're on the menu" by trying to restric Canada's trade policies with other nations. An abuser will try to isolate friends and family so you can only rely on them. I'm glad Canada walked away.
